append.text: Ps 64:7 *Prǽparans*, 64:10b *parásti … præparátio* → *Vós que preparais … preparastes … a sua preparação*: *præparáre* and *paráre* one verb, the noun its own (the psalm's play kept; MS1932's *Dás firmeza aos montes* interprets).

**Ps 64:8 *timébunt … a signis tuis* → *temerão os vossos sinais*** (the row's direct object); the Latinist asked for a causal phrase twice, minor, with two different fixes (*diante dos*, *por causa dos*) — both options.

**Ps 64:6 *Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster* → *Escutai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador*** — the test the row foresaw: the Greek is ὁ σωτήρ, the person, so *Salvador*; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.

**Ps 64:4 *impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis* → *vós sereis propício às nossas impiedades*** — applied as 24:11; the Latinist passed it twice, but **the blind reader heard God favouring our sins and listed *propício* as unknown** — the second reader to do so. Wants a ruling before 77:38, 78:9; *perdoareis* the option.

**Ps 64:5 departs: *quem elegísti, et assumpsísti* → *aquele que escolhestes e tomastes para vós*** — the Latinist's fix (προσελάβου), taken because all three readers stopped at *recolhestes* (sheltering; a jingle with *escolhestes*; gathering things up). *recolher* stays for a man drawn out of danger (17:17, 26:10); God taking a chosen man to himself is *tomar para si*.

**Ps 64:7 *Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia* → *Vós que preparais os montes com o vosso poder, cingido de potência*** — the instrumental *in* as *com* (the stylist heard *no vosso poder* as locative); the formula keeps *no* where it is locative (20:2, 53:3). *poténtia* in the same verse → *potência* (new row).

**Ps 64:8 *términos* alone (πέρατα, as 64:6 *fínium*) → *os confins*** — the stylist heard *os limites* as administrative and the blind reader as frontiers; one word with 64:6, by D15's Greek test. *os limites*, *os extremos* (the stylist) options.

**Ps 64:10 *inebriásti eam* → *a embriagastes*, 64:11 *Rivos ejus inébria* → *Embriagai os seus riachos*** — applied, one verb for both; the blind reader heard 'made drunk' as an odd metaphor (the Latin's). *inebriar*, *encharcar* options.
Ps 64:12 *campi tui replebúntur ubertáte* → *os vossos campos serão cheios de fartura* — applied, as the row foresaw; no remark.
Ps 64:12 *corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ* → *a coroa do ano da vossa benignidade* — held under D44 against the stylist's *bondade*; unknown to the blind reader again.
Ps 64:12 the noun *coróna anni* → *a coroa do ano* (the blind reader found the image unclear, as the Latin's).
Ps 64:14 *Indúti sunt aríetes óvium* → *Estão vestidos os carneiros das ovelhas* (not DRB's 'flock'); no reader objected to the genitive.

**Ps 64:13 *Pinguéscent speciósa desérti* → *Engordarão os lugares formosos do deserto*** — the verb of the family; the stylist's worst line (*engordar* comic) and *Ficarão fartos* is the option — refused because *fartos* is satiety (and echoes *fartura*, ubértas).
Ps 64:8 the causative *delectábis* → *alegrareis*, as 29:2 (the Greek differs, τέρψεις; the Latin verb and voice are the same); *deleitareis* the option.

Ps 64:14 *clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent* → *clamarão, pois hão de entoar um hino*: the blind reader heard *pois* as 'because' and the Latinist (v2, minor) called *étenim* intensive here (καὶ γάρ, 'yea') — held for the row; worth a look where *étenim* follows a verb it does not explain.

terms: | replére (passive) | encher: *ser cheio*, *estar cheio* (*Seremos cheios dos bens da vossa casa … O rio de Deus está cheio de águas … serão cheios de fartura*) | open | Ps 64:5b, 64:10b, 64:12 — one verb three times in one psalm, so one Portuguese verb, passive as the Latin; as 25:10 *repléta est → está cheia*. 62:6's jussive *repleátur → se farte* cannot serve 64:12 (*se fartarão de fartura*). Kept apart from *satiáre / saturáre → saciar*; shares *encher* with *adimplére* (two places). Pronominal *encher-se* the option. |

| poténtia | potência (*cingido de potência*) | open | Ps 64:7, where *virtus → poder* stands in the same verse (δυναστεία). *força* is fortitúdo's, *vigor* a man's virtus. *poderio* the option. Recurs (70:19 *Poténtiam tuam*, Ps 144 three times — grep all places before settling). |

| accíngere (passive) | cingir (*cingido de potência*; *as colinas serão cingidas de exultação*) | open | Ps 64:7, 64:13 — one verb, the psalm's echo kept; with *præcíngere → cingir* (17:33, 17:40). The blind reader listed *cingido(as)* as unknown; kept, the Latin's image. |

| locupletáre (*multiplicásti locupletáre eam*) | *multiplicastes a sua riqueza* | open | Ps 64:10 (ἐπλήθυνας τοῦ πλουτίσαι): *multiplicar* kept (it returns in 64:11), the infinitive made a noun. The Latinist asked *multiplicastes o enriquecê-la* twice (minor) — not said in Portuguese; option, with DRB's *de muitos modos a enriquecestes*. The stylist named it the psalm's best line. |
| rivus | riacho (*Embriagai os seus riachos*) | open | Ps 64:11 (the Greek αὔλακας 'furrows' not followed). *regatos* (DM1962's word here), *ribeiros* (MS1932) options. |

| genímina | colheitas (*multiplicai as suas colheitas*) | open | Ps 64:11 (γενήματα); kept apart from *fructus → fruto* (καρπός). The only place in the psalter (grep). *frutos*, *produtos* options. |
| stillicídium | gota (*com as suas gotas*) | open | Ps 64:11 (σταγόνες); 71:6 *sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram* should follow. |

| gérminans (substantive) | *o que germina* | open | Ps 64:11 *lætábitur gérminans*: the v1 Latinist, the stylist and the blind reader read it as the subject; the v2 Latinist asked back the gerund *germinando* (draft 1) — the runs contradict, for Gustavo. *o que brota* (the stylist) option. |

| speciósa (neuter plural, substantive) | os lugares formosos (*os lugares formosos do deserto*) | open | Ps 64:13 (τὰ ὡραῖα), the Latinist's fix after draft 1's *as belezas* drifted to an abstraction; DRB 'the beautiful places'. The supplied noun is the cost. |

| indúere (perfect passive, no object named) | *estar vestido* (*Estão vestidos os carneiros das ovelhas*) | open | Ps 64:14: the resulting state, as 25:10 *repléta est*; what they are clothed with left unsaid, as the Latin. The Latinist (v2, minor) asked *Vestiram-se* (past, but middle voice) — option. |

| hymnum dícere | entoar um hino (*hão de entoar um hino*) | open | Ps 64:14, after *psalmum dícere → entoar um salmo* (17:50, 26:6b, 56:8, 60:9); *cantar* is cantáre's. The periphrastic future to avoid three *-arão* in one verse (the stylist), as 29:9. |

| éxitus matutíni, et véspere | as saídas da manhã, e à tarde (*alegrareis as saídas da manhã, e à tarde*) | open | Ps 64:8: *véspere* is an ablative in form ('at evening'), the Latinist's v2 fix, against the Greek's two genitives (ἐξόδους πρωίας καὶ ἑσπέρας) and DRB's symmetrical pair, which is the option. The blind reader found *saídas* opaque (exits); it is the Latin's crux, left concrete. |
| collis | colina (*as colinas serão cingidas de exultação*) | open | Ps 64:13; *outeiro* (MS1932) dated. 71:3, 113:4, 113:6, 148:9 (grep) should follow. |

Spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe* (Special/Preces.txt, 64:6b) · *Visitásti terram et inebriásti eam, multiplicásti locupletáre eam* (missa Sancti/02-11) | *A vós convém o hino, Deus, em Sião: * e a vós será pago o voto em Jerusalém* · *Escutai, Senhor, a minha oração: * a vós virá toda a carne* · *R. Esperança de todos os confins da terra, e no mar, ao longe.* · *Visitastes a terra, e a embriagastes: multiplicastes a sua riqueza* | open — Ps 64; the antiphon divides after *o hino* as the Latin after *hymnus*; the Te Deum close *te decet hymnus* (Common/Prayers.txt) should say *a vós convém o hino* too |
